title: The unit-compatible comparison is injective on neighbourhood colimits
statement: Let $X$ and $Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Write $b_i:X_{\Et}\to Z_{\Et}$ for base change, $i^*F$ for its sheaf inverse image with adjunction unit $\eta^{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], and $j_X,j_Z$ for the open-subscheme inclusion functors. Suppose $A$ and $G$ are topological sheaves of sets on $X$ and $Z$, with presheaf isomorphisms $e_X:A\cong F\circ j_X$ and $e_Z:G\cong (i^*F)\circ j_Z$. For each open $W\subseteq X$, choose an isomorphism $a_W:j_Z(i^{-1}W)\cong b_i(j_X(W))$ of etale $Z$-schemes whose first pullback projection is the restricted morphism $i|_W:i^{-1}W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define the function $r_W:A(W)\to G(i^{-1}W)$ by $r_W(s)=e_Z^{-1}((i^*F)(a_W)(\eta^{\Et}_{j_X(W)}(e_X(s))))$, where $(i^*F)(a_W)$ denotes contravariant restriction along the hom of $a_W$. Let $L=i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}A$ be the topological sheaf inverse image, with unit $\eta^{\rm Zar}$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. If $\beta:L\to G$ is any morphism of sheaves such that $\beta_{i^{-1}W}(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(s))=r_W(s)$ for every $W,s$, then for every $z\in Z$ the induced function $\varinjlim_{V\ni z}L(V)\to\varinjlim_{V\ni z}G(V)$ is injective, where both colimits range over open neighbourhoods ordered by reverse inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk].

proof.text: Fix z and two elements of the inverse-image stalk. Represent both as unit germs of sections a and b on one open W containing i(z).

Apply colimit.ι_map to the assumed equality of beta images. The filtered-colimit equality criterion produces an open V around z on which the two image sections agree. Rewrite them by the given unit equation hbeta.
Apply local agreement to get W0 contained in W around i(z), on which a and b restrict equally.

Naturality of the topological unit gives equality of the unit sections after restriction to i^{-1}W0. The neighbourhood-colimit relations identify their germs with the original two elements, which are therefore equal.
